directAnswer: To check a URL shortener, you can use online tools that reveal the original URL or check the URL's destination directly in your browser.
summary: This guide provides steps to verify shortened URLs and highlights important considerations.

sections.heading: Understanding URL Shorteners
sections.body: URL shorteners create a compact version of a long URL. They can obscure the destination, making it essential to verify them before clicking.

sections.heading: Using Online Tools
sections.body: Several online services can help you expand shortened URLs safely without visiting them directly.

sections.heading: Manual Checking
sections.body: You can also manually check the destination by copying the shortened URL and pasting it into a URL expander tool.

steps.title: Use a URL expander service
steps.detail: Visit a URL expander website, such as CheckShortURL or Unshorten.It, and paste the shortened URL into the provided field.

steps.title: Check the link in your browser
steps.detail: Copy the shortened URL, paste it into your browser's address bar, and add a '+' at the end (for bit.ly links) to see the original URL.

steps.title: Use browser extensions
steps.detail: Install a browser extension designed to preview shortened URLs before clicking, such as 'Unshorten.link' for Chrome.

faqs.question: Are all URL shorteners safe?
faqs.answer: Not all URL shorteners are safe; some may lead to malicious sites. Always verify before clicking.

faqs.question: Can I trust URL expander tools?
faqs.answer: Most URL expander tools are reliable, but ensure you use well-known services to avoid phishing attempts.

faqs.question: What should I do if a shortened URL looks suspicious?
faqs.answer: Avoid clicking on it and use a URL expander tool to check the destination safely.

caveats: Some URL shorteners may not allow expansion for privacy reasons.
URL shorteners can change their policies, affecting how links are handled.
